Unit 7: ML Preprocessing & Math

HL curriculum overview and structured learning plan.

Introduction

Why is most data useless for AI?

This unit focuses on Data Fidelity and Mathematics. You will learn that 80% of Machine Learning is just cleaning data (Preprocessing). We will cover how to handle missing values, normalize scales, and perform the foundational math of Linear Regression ($y=mx+c$).

You'll start by cleaning a messy dataset (Imputation, Outliers). Then you'll transform it for the machine (One-Hot Encoding, Scaling). Finally, you'll open the 'Black Box' of AI to understand the math behind Cost Functions and Gradient Descent.

Data Cleaning (Garbage In, Garbage Out)

If you feed an AI bad data, you get bad predictions.

  • Noise: Random errors or irrelevant data.
  • Imputation: filling in missing values (e.g., using the average).
  • Outliers: Extreme values that warp the model (e.g., a house costing $1 Billion).
Feature Engineering

Making data easier for the machine to understand.

  • One-Hot Encoding: Converting categories (Red, Blue) into numbers (0, 1).
  • Normalization: Squishing data into a range (0 to 1) so large numbers don't dominate.
  • Dimensionality Reduction: Removing useless columns to speed up learning.
Linear Regression (The Math)

The simplest form of Machine Learning.

  • Formula: $y = mx + c$ (Line of Best Fit).
  • Cost Function (MSE): A way to calculate "How wrong is the line?"
  • Gradient Descent: The algorithm that nudges the line until errors are minimized.
Key Terminology
TermDefinition
Preprocessing The process of preparing raw data for a machine learning model (cleaning, formatting).
Imputation Replacing missing data with substituted values (e.g., mean, median).
Outlier A data point that differs significantly from other observations.
One-Hot Encoding Converting categorical data variables into a form that could be provided to ML algorithms (Binary columns).
Normalization Rescaling numeric attributes to a common range, usually 0 to 1.
Linear Regression An algorithm that models the relationship between two variables by fitting a linear equation.
Mean Squared Error (MSE) A cost function that measures the average of the squares of the errors (difference between predicted and actual).
Gradient Descent An optimization algorithm used to minimize the cost function by iteratively moving towards the steepest descent.
